Distributed Joins

1. Colocated vs. Non-Colocated Joins
  • When two tables are joined, the data from both tables must be on the same node to perform the join locally;
  • Colocated join — both tables use the same affinity key, so related rows live on the same node; the join is performed locally on each node and results are merged;
  • Non-colocated (distributed) join — tables have different affinity keys; data must be shuffled across the network to perform the join;
2. How Colocated Joins Work
  • If Customer is partitioned by customerId and Order is also affinity-colocated by customerId: 
    -- This join is fully local on each node
SELECT c.name, o.amount
FROM Customer c
JOIN Order o ON c.customerId = o.customerId;
  • Each node joins only its local data, then results are sent back to the query originator;
  • Fast and scalable — no data shuffling;
3. How Non-Colocated Joins Work
  • If the joined tables are not colocated, Ignite must broadcast parts of one table to all nodes;
  • Must be explicitly enabled: 
    SqlFieldsQuery query = new SqlFieldsQuery(
    "SELECT p.name, d.deptName FROM Person p JOIN Department d ON p.deptId = d.id"
);
query.setDistributedJoins(true);
  • Or via JDBC: 
    jdbc:ignite:thin://host:10800?distributedJoins=true
4. Performance Implications
AspectColocated JoinNon-Colocated Join
Network trafficMinimalHigh (data shuffling)
LatencyLowHigh
ScalabilityLinear with nodesLimited by network
ConfigurationRequires affinity colocation setupJust enable distributedJoins
5. Joins with REPLICATED Tables
  • Joining a PARTITIONED table with a REPLICATED table is always local — every node has the full replicated data;
  • This is a common pattern: keep small lookup tables (country codes, categories) as REPLICATED and large transactional tables as PARTITIONED;
6. Best Practices
  • Design your data model to use affinity colocation for frequently joined tables;
  • Use REPLICATED mode for small lookup/reference tables;
  • Avoid non-colocated joins on large tables in latency-sensitive paths;
  • Use EXPLAIN to analyze join strategies;
